crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: FAIR Data
children.blurb: FAIR data describes research outputs that are findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable by both people and machines.

children.name: Metadata and Ontologies
children.blurb: Metadata and ontologies give research data repositories the descriptive structure needed to make datasets findable, comparable, and reusable across disciplines.

children.name: Federated Sharing of Sensitive Data
children.blurb: Federated sharing of sensitive data covers methods for research institutions to jointly analyze or train models on restricted datasets without moving raw records to a central repository.

children.name: Institutional Knowledge Graphs
children.blurb: An institutional knowledge graph is a structured representation of the entities and relationships that matter to a research organization, such as people, publications, datasets, projects, grants, equipment, and organizational units.

children.name: Long-Term Digital Preservation
children.blurb: Long-term digital preservation in research data and repositories concerns keeping digital objects readable, usable, and authentic beyond the life of the software, hardware, and institutions that created them.

sections.body: This field is about making research data findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable, the FAIR principles. Artificial intelligence is now doing concrete work here: extracting structured claims from papers, linking datasets to ontologies, generating metadata, and matching records across repositories. It is not a future promise; systems already parse PDFs, label variables, and build knowledge graphs from institutional records. The site's own library of 10,767 extracted claims from research works is an example of the kind of structured output this field produces. AI also helps with de-identification for sensitive data sharing and with format migration for preservation.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The basics of metadata extraction and ontology alignment are reasonably mature for clean, well-formatted inputs. What is not solved is messy, domain-specific, or cross-institutional data where standards conflict or are missing. Federated sharing of sensitive data remains hard because privacy guarantees, consent tracking, and audit logs are still research problems, not settled engineering. Long-term preservation is also limited: AI can help migrate file formats and check integrity, but it cannot yet guarantee semantic usability decades later. Honest limits include poor recall on rare entity types, bias in automated metadata, and the fact that many repositories still rely on manual curation.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader wanting the core principles should start with FAIR Data, which explains the four requirements and how AI tools assess them. Metadata and Ontologies goes deeper into the vocabularies and schemas that make those principles operational, and it is the page to consult for how AI extracts and aligns terms. Federated Sharing of Sensitive Data addresses the harder case of data that cannot be centralized, covering privacy-preserving queries and distributed learning. Institutional Knowledge Graphs shows how a single organization can connect its people, projects, datasets, and outputs into one queryable structure. Long-Term Digital Preservation closes the loop by asking what happens to all of this in ten or fifty years, and what AI can and cannot do to keep it readable.
